newsitem.title: POLAND: Daiwa sees Warsaw WIG index at 14,100 at year-end.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa sees Warsaw WIG index at 14,100 at year-end.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse is likely to gain only marginally this month and its main WIG index should close at 14,100 points at the end of the year, Daiwa Europe Ltd said in its December report.
"Having already seen gains of 82 percent (57 percent in dollar terms) so far this year, both foreign and domestic investors are likely to remain subdued until the new year," the report said.
The WIG slipped from 13,789.7 points on November 29, when the report was dated, to 13,322.5 points on Monday.
The report maintained an overweight position recommendation for the Polish market while suggesting a slightly more neutral stance on the Polish shares.
It said the market drop had brought down valuations for several key companies, which provided attractive buying opportunities.
"Although we are slightly more neutral on Polish shares, we still maintain an overweight stance and see an end-1997 index target of 17,500," it said.
The market has already fallen 11.6 percent since recording a high of 15,078.7 points on October 9.
The report warned that investors' interest was likely to be pulled away from the secondary market in 1997, with large privatisations planned in the second quarter of the year.
It also said that parliamentary elections, scheduled for late 1997, were likely to increase political uncertainty and dampen investor sentiment.
